title: Christina Myalla
text:
I am a Research Data Scientist at the Malaria Atlas Project (MAP) East Africa Node, based at Ifakara Health Institute in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, with a joint affiliation to The Kids Research Institute Australia. I lead the Node’s Data Engineering Team and coordinate MAP’s Geospatial Modelling training programme.
My work turns messy, multi-source health data into spatial evidence that health programmes can act on. I build reproducible pipelines that harmonise health facility data across sub-Saharan Africa, model how long it takes people to reach care, and measure how climate hazards such as floods disrupt that access. I then package the results as dashboards and portals for National Malaria Control Programmes.
Before MAP, I spent over a decade managing data for clinical trials and cohort studies in Tanzania, including household GPS data collection, multi-country trial databases and data quality systems.

text:
Coordinator, Geospatial Modelling for Public Health Applications Workshop (MAP, 2024 to present)
An annual workshop on spatial modelling with INLA, now in its third cohort, drawing hundreds of applicants and participants from over seven African countries. I also built the reproducible selection pipeline used to choose each cohort.

Trainer, AMMnet Tanzania “Introduction to R Training” (October 2026)
Taught reproducible workflows with R Markdown to about 30 students, lecturers and public health specialists. Received a Certificate of Appreciation.
Earlier teaching
Trained data clerks, data managers and research nurses in database practice (MITU, MUHAS), and lectured in computing at the University of Dar es Salaam.

title: Projects
text:
Conference presentations 2026


How much longer does it take to reach a health facility when rivers flood? I combined JRC GloFAS flood hazard maps, OpenStreetMap road networks and travel-time modelling across about 11,900 essential health facilities to identify the facilities and districts where flooding cuts people off from care.

title: Projects
text:
Data products and dashboards


Live

HealthScope
A health facility intelligence portal for sub-Saharan Africa. It sits on an ETL pipeline I designed that harmonises national facility lists into the Sub-Saharan Africa Harmonised Health Facility Database (about 78,000 facilities and 300,000 service records, stored in DuckDB and GeoParquet), with tabs on services, access and population reach.
Visit HealthScope
R · DuckDB · GeoParquet · Quarto · GitHub Actions



Country dashboards

Malaria risk dashboards
Interactive dashboards for National Malaria Control Programmes that bring crude, adjusted and modelled malaria incidence and prevalence together with environmental covariates and seasonality, ending in composite risk maps for sub-national tailoring.
View the Benin dashboard

Also built for Burkina Faso and Mozambique.
R Shiny · bslib · WHO SNT indicators



Training tools

Modelling transparency dashboards
Three training dashboards (Mozambique, Angola, Benin) that walk programme staff step by step through how MAP produces its malaria estimates, from routine data to modelled outputs.

R Shiny · Quarto



In development

Malaria country profiles portal
A standardised, open-access Quarto portal summarising malaria epidemiology, environmental and entomological data for 11 African countries. Researchers submit data through GitHub, and automated workflows rebuild the site.
Quarto · GitHub Actions · R



In development

WapiCare: nearest health facility finder
A mobile web app for Tanzania’s flood season. A user shares their location and gets the nearest health facility, the route by transport mode and the services available there. I lead the project and own data preparation.
PWA · routing · health facility data
